title: Drowning
stem: Resus 2. A 16-year-old boy was pulled from a public pool after an unknown time under water. The lifeguard started CPR. He arrives with CPR in progress; the monitor shows asystole. Temperature 35.0 °C.
notes:
Checked against the ERC 2021 guidelines (drowning), Resuscitation Council UK 2021 and ILCOR.

Drowning arrest is hypoxic. Open the airway and give 5 initial rescue breaths (ERC) before compressions, then 30:2. AHA gives 2 initial breaths; your notes say 2 or 3–5. The station scores the ERC 5.

Do not try to drain water from the lungs (no Heimlich or abdominal thrusts): it delays ventilation and causes aspiration of vomit. Expect vomit; suction and turn only if needed. Intubate early; the lungs are stiff and need PEEP.

Spinal precautions only if there is a history of diving, a high-energy mechanism or signs of injury; routine collars impede the airway. Your notes agree.

Hypothermia: below 30 °C withhold adrenaline and give at most 3 shocks; between 30 and 35 °C double the drug interval. Rewarm actively. After ROSC, prevent fever (keep below 37.7 °C for 72 hours). Your notes say 'therapeutic hypothermia'; current ERC–ESICM guidance moved from cooling to 32–36 °C toward fever prevention.

Salt versus fresh water makes no clinical difference. Antibiotics only for grossly contaminated water or clinical infection.

steps.label: Lifeguard
steps.hint: How long under, diving?, what was done, when.

Event.r: Not sure — maybe 5 minutes. He was found at the bottom of the deep end.

Event.t: Did he dive in or hit anything?
Event.r: No diving there. No marks on him.
Event.mark: Asks about diving or trauma (spinal risk)

Event.t: What did you do and when?
Event.r: Pulled him out, no breathing, gave rescue breaths and CPR at once. Water came up. About 15 minutes of CPR.
Event.mark: Asks what CPR was done and for how long

steps.label: Resuscitate
steps.hint: Airway and suction, 5 rescue breaths, 30:2, rhythm, adrenaline, intubate early.

opts.t: Open the airway and suction the vomit
Five rescue breaths with bag-mask and oxygen
IV or IO access; adrenaline 1 mg now, then every 3–5 min (temperature above 35)
opts.mark: Adrenaline at the right interval for his temperature

opts.t: Next rhythm check: organised rhythm with a pulse
opts.r: Sinus tachycardia 118 with a palpable femoral pulse.

opts.t: Abdominal thrusts to empty the lungs first
opts.r: Delays ventilation and causes vomiting and aspiration.

opts.t: Put a rigid collar on before anything else
opts.r: No diving or trauma history: a collar only obstructs the airway.

steps.label: After ROSC
steps.hint: Oxygenate with PEEP, targets, temperature, stomach, investigations.

opts.t: Keep the temperature below 37.7 °C for 72 hours; rewarm gently to normal
Nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach
Keep him at 32 °C for 24 hours routinely
opts.r: Current post-arrest guidance prevents fever rather than routinely cooling to 32–36.

opts.t: Start IV antibiotics routinely for pool water
opts.r: Only for grossly contaminated water or signs of infection.

Tests.r: Tube in a good position. Bilateral patchy perihilar shadowing (aspiration and non-cardiogenic oedema).
pH 7.08, PaCO2 7.9, PaO2 8.2 on FiO2 1.0, lactate 9.

Tests.mark: 12-lead ECG (arrhythmia, long QT as a cause)

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Paediatric or adult ICU; talk to the family.

opts.t: ICU: 16, drowning, 15 min CPR, ROSC, ventilated on PEEP 10, FiO2 1.0
opts.mark: Refers to ICU with a clear summary

opts.t: Discharge after 6 hours if he wakes
opts.r: He needed CPR and is ventilated. ICU.

qs.q: ERC: how many initial rescue breaths in drowning?
When are spinal precautions needed in drowning?
qs.a: Diving, high-energy mechanism or signs of injury

qs.q: Salt water versus fresh water drowning?

badge.name: Lifeguard
badge.flavor: Five breaths first. Hypoxia caused it; oxygen fixes it.

cards.q: In drowning arrest, ERC recommends starting with…
Abdominal thrusts to remove water in drowning are…
cards.why: They delay ventilation and cause aspiration.

cards.q: Core temperature at which adrenaline is withheld in hypothermic arrest?
cards.why: Between 30 and 35 °C, double the dosing interval.

options: Cool to 32 °C for 24 h in all

cards.q: Routine C-spine immobilisation after drowning is…
options: Not indicated without diving or injury
Required if the water was cold
cards.why: Spinal injury is rare without diving or trauma.

cards.q: Typical chest X-ray after significant drowning?
cards.why: Aspiration and surfactant loss cause ARDS-like changes.
